raw_response:
I've been growing chili on this same ground for as long as I can remember. My mother grew it here too. 2.6 mu is not much, but it feeds us and gives us some money. I know chili. I don't need to think too hard about this — I'll do what I always do, with small adjustments from what I learned last year.

I'll start seedlings indoors in late February, in a warm corner of the house with some plastic sheeting over the bed. I buy hybrid seeds from the seed shop in town — I stopped saving my own seeds maybe ten years ago when those hybrid ones started giving me more fruit and the plants looked healthier. They cost more but I get it back at harvest.

In early March I'll rotary till the whole plot. The soil here compacts over winter and needs breaking up. I'll mix in the base fertilizer then — diammonium phosphate and some compound fertilizer. I won't measure it exactly, I'll just spread it the way I've always done.

Transplanting goes in April, after the last frost. Once the plants take hold, I'll water from the well. Summer is hot and dry here, I'll water often — maybe ten times total. I watch the leaves; when they start to droop in the morning that's when I know it's time.

I'll spray pesticide when I see aphids or when neighbors tell me there's something going around. Usually six or seven times gets through the season without losing too much.

I expect around 500 jin per mu on a normal year — maybe a little more if the rains cooperate.
